newsitem.title: ISRAEL: FORECAST-Israel trade deficit to widen 10.7 pct.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Israel trade deficit to widen 10.7 pct.

text.p: Israel's trade deficit excluding diamonds will widen 10.7 percent in 1996 to $11.4 billion from $10.3 billion last year, the Israel Export Institute forecast on Monday.
Exports, excluding diamonds, will grow only 4.4 percent this year to $14 billion from $13.4 billion in 1995, the institute's chairman Amir Makov told a news conference.
This compares with 10.7 percent growth in exports last year and an average of 12 percent annual growth from 1991 to 1995.
The largest part of the deficit is with the European Union. In 1995 Israel's deficit with the EU reached $6.5 billion.
Makov blamed the slowdown in export growth to a decline in profitability, the result of an overvalued shekel, he said.
The institute said exports to the United States in 1996 will decline 3.6 percent while growth in exports to the EU and Asia will slow significantly because of the exchange rate.
Growth in exports to Russia and republics of the former Soviet Union is also expected to slow.

The institute also expressed concern that growth in Israeli exports was not keeping pace with growth in trade worldwide. According to the International Monetary Fund's World Economic Outlook, world trade is expected to grow 6.2 percent in 1996.

The institute said small and medium size exporters prefer to sell their goods in the U.S. market. About 60 percent of small and medium size high-tech companies, for example, export mainly to the United States against 16 percent to the EU.
As a result, the deficit with the EU is likely to widen, the institute predicted.
Figures from the institute show that in the past five years telecommunications equipment and electronic components have led the expansion in Israel's industrial exports.
Exports of telecommunications equipment accounted for 27 percent of the growth in exports while electronic components accounted for 13 percent.
The two sectors combined account for 31 percent of Israel's industrial exports against 23 percent in 1991.
